questions.question: For a pulsar slowing down due to rotational energy loss, the braking index is defined as n = Ω (d²Ω/dt²) / (dΩ/dt)², where Ω is the angular rotation frequency. Pure magnetic dipole radiation in a vacuum yields a theoretical braking index of n = 3. Why do young pulsars, such as the Crab Pulsar, systematically exhibit observed braking indices of n < 3?
options: Quantum electrodynamic photon splitting suppresses the dipole radiation field at ultra-high magnetic field strengths.
The neutron star expands rapidly due to thermal pressure, increasing its moment of inertia.
Additional torque is exerted by a relativistic magnetospheric particle wind, or the pulsar's magnetic dipole moment increases over time.
Gravitational wave radiation from quadrupolar deformations dominates over magnetic dipole torque.

questions.question: In the theory of stellar atmospheres, the Rosseland mean opacity κ_R is defined so that the frequency-integrated radiative energy flux in an optically thick medium matches the flux derived from radiative transfer equations. Which function acts as the weighting factor when integrating the inverse monochromatic opacity (1/κ_ν) over frequency to calculate 1/κ_R?
options: The temperature derivative of the Planck function, ∂B_ν(T)/∂T
The Planck function itself, B_ν(T)
The exponential optical depth factor, exp(-τ_ν)
The frequency derivative of the local source function, ∂S_ν/∂ν

questions.question: Low-mass main-sequence stars (M < 2 M_sun) eventually experience a core helium flash at the tip of the Red Giant Branch. What fundamental property of the core's state prevents immediate, stable thermal expansion upon helium ignition, leading to this explosive runaway?
options: Thermal pressure dominates the core, causing instantaneous heating without volume change.
Non-relativistic electron degeneracy pressure supports the core and is independent of temperature, preventing cooling via thermal expansion.
Neutrino cooling suddenly drops to zero at ignition, trapping all energy generated by the triple-alpha process.
Radiative transfer breaks down completely, causing acoustic resonance that exponentially amplifies fusion.

questions.question: In optical and radio interferometry, the van Cittert-Zernike theorem provides the foundational mathematical link between spatial coherence and image formation. According to this theorem, what is the complex visibility measured on a baseline related to?
options: The 2D spatial distribution of line-of-sight magnetic field strength via Faraday rotation.
The 1D radial velocity dispersion profile of the target via a Hilbert transform.
The spatial correlation coefficient of atmospheric seeing disks as a function of optical depth.
The 2D brightness intensity distribution of the observed source on the sky via a 2D Fourier transform.

questions.question: In active galactic nuclei (AGN) reverberation mapping, astronomers measure the time lag Δt between variability in the central continuum flux and the corresponding response of broad emission lines. What physical quantity is directly determined from this time lag?
options: The mass accretion rate onto the supermassive black hole.
The inclination angle of the AGN accretion disk relative to the line of sight.
The characteristic physical radius of the Broad Line Region from the central ionizing source.
The dimensionless Kerr spin parameter of the central supermassive black hole.
